title: Predict string allocation and equality behavior and distinguish UTF-16 code units from user-perceived characters

rubric.point: States that strings are immutable, so `ToUpper()` cannot modify the existing string object that `name` refers to.
Explains that `ToUpper()` returns a new string, and because that result is not assigned (for example back to `name`), `name` still refers to the original `"ada"` object.

questions.model: `string` is immutable, so `ToUpper()` cannot change the `"ada"` object. Instead it returns a new string `"ADA"`. That return value is discarded because it is never assigned, so `name` still refers to the original `"ada"`. Writing `name = name.ToUpper();` would make `name` refer to the new string.
